scope: Literature-traced scalar quantities read out of published primary sources by an agent in this repository. Every value here was read from a source the agent actually opened: the source text or supplementary table is quoted or the exact cell is named. Nothing here is a bench measurement made in this work package, and nothing here is a checksummed upstream file living in the repository.

availability_vocabulary.literature_traced: The agent opened the primary source, located the value, and recorded the exact locator (table, cell, or quoted sentence). The source file is NOT vendored in this repository. This is strictly weaker than local_verified and must never be recorded as local_verified.
availability_vocabulary.derived_composite: Not measured by any single source. Computed here from two or more literature_traced inputs that come from different strains, media, growth modes or laboratories. The splice is named in every such entry.
availability_vocabulary.unresolved: Searched for and not found, or found only behind a paywall with no accessible mirror. The search that was run is recorded so it is not repeated blindly.

merge_notes: If this run introduces a differently-named availability level for our own artifacts, rename literature_traced to it rather than adding a second vocabulary.
No file under data/parameter_evidence.json was edited by this agent. The corrections in repository_corrections_recommended are reports, not changes.

The two supplementary spreadsheets under sources.kumar_bruheim2021.remote_artifacts were downloaded and read but deliberately NOT vendored, because vendoring is outside this agent's file ownership. Their sha256 digests are recorded so a later agent can pin them and promote the entry to a verified level.

kumar_bruheim2021.title: Large dependency of intracellular NAD and CoA pools on cultivation conditions in Saccharomyces cerevisiae

verification.locator: Additional file 1 (13104_2021_5783_MOESM1_ESM.xlsx), sheet 'NADs+CoAs_n=2', row 'G lim' / growth rate 0.05, column group 'Acetyl CoA'. The article text names this file as 'Additional file 1: Table S1'.
verification.finding: Acetyl-CoA at G lim, D = 0.05 h^-1 is 19.9044 nmol/gDW, the mean of two replicas at 18.683272 and 21.125529 nmol/gDW, relative standard deviation 8.676157 percent. This is the origin of the repository's 0.0199 umol/gDW.

remote_artifacts.contents: Per-replica absolute pools, nmoles per gram biomass, for NAD, NADH, NADP, NADPH, FAD, CoA, acetyl-CoA and succinyl-CoA across 21 cultivations.
Sheets 'All' and 'Modes': condition-averaged pools joined to glucose, growth rate, ethanol, O2 and CO2 rates, plus per-mode slope and r-square against growth rate.

culture.aeration: minimum dissolved oxygen level of 40 percent, so aerobic
culture.mode: carbon-limited chemostat, low-glucose feed 1.0 g/L (rows 'Glim'); a separate high-glucose 10.0 g/L series is labelled 'GlimHi'

quench_and_extraction.quoted: the standard sampling protocols with fast filtration, freeze-thaw extraction, and concentration by freeze-drying can't be applied, but pelleting using centrifugation and snap freezing had to be used
quench_and_extraction.coa_extraction: acetonitrile:methanol:water (70:10:20, v/v/v) containing 50 mM ammonium acetate pH 5.0
quench_and_extraction.platform: two HILIC-MS/MS methods with 13C internal standard dilution

author_reported_limitations: the small sample size (two replicas) is the main limitation of the study since it was based on leftover samples from a large study with 22 different cultivation conditions
This preliminary investigation reveals no correlation between growth rate and pool sizes

kozak2016.title: Replacement of the initial steps of ethanol metabolism in Saccharomyces cerevisiae by ATP-independent acetylating acetaldehyde dehydrogenase
kozak2016.authors: Kozak BU, van Rossum HM, Niemeijer MS, van Dijk M, Benjamin K, Wu L, Daran J-MG, Pronk JT, van Maris AJA
kozak2016.pmid_note: Europe PMC returns 26818854 for this DOI. One secondary rendering returned 26819129; 26818854 is the value carried by the Europe PMC record that also carries the DOI and PMCID, and is the one recorded here.

verification.locator: Results, 'Physiology of evolved Ald- A-ALD-dependent strains in ethanol-limited chemostat cultures', quoted below; the same value is carried in Table 8 (Steady-state intracellular metabolite concentrations, umol g dry weight^-1) and Table S4.
verification.finding: Quoted verbatim: 'intracellular acetyl-CoA concentrations in the evolved strain (0.83 +/- 0.17 umol g dry weight-1) and reference strain (0.85 +/- 0.27 umol g dry weight-1) were not significantly different'. The 0.85 is the reference strain CEN.PK113-7D. This is the origin of the repository's 0.85 umol/gDW.

culture.medium: synthetic medium (Verduyn et al. 1992), ingoing ethanol 6 g/L
culture.aeration: aerobic 2-L bioreactor, 1 L working volume, sparged
culture.mode: ethanol-limited chemostat; steady-state samples taken between 12 and 15 volume changes
culture.dilution_rate_note: Table 7 reports 0.048 +/- 0.001 h^-1 against a nominal setpoint of 0.05 h^-1
culture.compartment: whole cell; Table 8 is titled 'intracellular', and the paper reports no compartment-resolved acetyl-CoA

quench_and_extraction.quoted: Chemostat cultures were sampled for determination of intracellular metabolite concentrations according to the cold methanol quenching method using specially designed rapid sampling setup (Lange et al. 2001). Approximately 1.2 mL of broth was sampled into 5 mL of 80% aqueous methanol (v/v) solution pre-cooled to -40C. Subsequently, samples were washed with cold methanol followed by extraction of intracellular metabolites with boiling ethanol as described by Canelas et al. (2008).
quench_and_extraction.platform: ion-pair reverse-phase LC-MS/MS (Van Dam et al. 2002) for CoA and acetyl-CoA, with uniformly 13C-labelled cell extracts as internal standards (Wu et al. 2005)

acetyl_coa_provenance.verdict: RESOLVED. Both numbers are traceable and both were read at source. The 42.7-fold gap is NOT a compartment difference and NOT a unit difference: both values are whole-cell contents in umol/gDW, in the same strain, in the same medium family, at the same nominal dilution rate, both aerobic chemostats. The gap is a carbon-source contrast CONFOUNDED with a laboratory, quench, extraction and analytical-platform change, and the two numbers must not be differenced.

the_two_numbers.0.0199_umol_per_gdw: Kumar K & Bruheim P, BMC Res Notes 14:361 (2021), doi 10.1186/s13104-021-05783-6, PMID 34556160. Additional file 1, sheet 'NADs+CoAs_n=2', row G lim / 0.05. Published as 19.9044 nmol/gDW, mean of 18.683272 and 21.125529, relative SD 8.68 percent, n = 2.
the_two_numbers.0.85_umol_per_gdw: Kozak BU, van Rossum HM et al., FEMS Yeast Res 16(2):fow006 (2016), doi 10.1093/femsyr/fow006, PMID 26818854. Table 8 / Results text. 0.85 +/- 0.27 umol/gDW, n = 3.

what_the_repository_got_right: The comment in scripts/thiolase_threshold.py that both come from the same strain (CEN.PK113-7D), the same medium (Verduyn) and the same dilution rate (0.05 /h) is CORRECT. All three checked out against both sources.
The locator 'supplementary Table S1' for the glucose number is CORRECT: the article itself names the file 'Additional file 1: Table S1'.
The standing caveat that two laboratories with two quench protocols was never a number to build on is CORRECT, and is now demonstrated rather than asserted.

what_the_repository_got_wrong.note: The string 'Kolbeinsen' appears nowhere in the paper, in its author list, or in any Bruheim-lab yeast publication found by search. This is why the number read as untraceable: the value and the locator were right and the name was not.

what_the_repository_got_wrong.where: scripts/thiolase_threshold.py:75 ('Measured cytosolic acetyl-CoA'), src/ystwin/pathway/thermo_gate.py:16-17 ('Measured cytosolic acetyl-CoA is about 10 uM on glucose and 425 uM on ethanol'), and the same phrasing in the module docstring at scripts/thiolase_threshold.py:19
what_the_repository_got_wrong.correct: Both sources report INTRACELLULAR, i.e. whole-cell, content per gram dry weight. Neither is compartment-resolved. Kozak's Table 8 is titled 'Steady-state intracellular metabolite concentrations'; Kumar & Bruheim measure whole-cell pellets.
what_the_repository_got_wrong.consequence: Dividing a whole-cell pool by a CYTOSOLIC volume OVERSTATES the cytosolic concentration, because part of the pool sits in mitochondria and peroxisomes. The current practice therefore errs toward declaring the thiolase step feasible, which is the conservative direction for a refutation but the wrong direction for any future claim that the step runs.

protocol_difference.kozak2016: leakage-free rapid quenching: 1.2 mL broth into 5 mL 80 percent aqueous methanol pre-cooled to -40 C via a dedicated rapid-sampling setup (Lange 2001), cold-methanol wash, boiling-ethanol extraction (Canelas 2008), ion-pair reverse-phase LC-MS/MS with U-13C internal standards.
protocol_difference.kumar_bruheim2021: pelleting by centrifugation followed by snap freezing, chosen because fast filtration and freeze-thaw could not be applied to these unstable analytes; cold organic extraction; HILIC-MS/MS with 13C internal standards.
protocol_difference.significance: These differ in the step that matters most for a fast-turnover thioester. A centrifugation is orders of magnitude slower than a -40 C methanol quench.

cross_laboratory_anchors_are_inconsisten.method: Compare metabolites the two papers both report, whole-cell umol/gDW, CEN.PK113-7D, D approx 0.05. Kozak Table 8 lists only fold-change >= 2 metabolites, so the overlap is small.
cross_laboratory_anchors_are_inconsisten.reading: There is no single scale factor that reconciles the two datasets. NADH agrees within 1.4-fold while NADPH, F1,6BP and acetyl-CoA all sit 32 to 43-fold apart in the SAME direction. A uniform laboratory offset would move NADH too; a genuine carbon-source effect would not move F1,6BP the wrong way, since fructose-1,6-bisphosphate is expected HIGHER on glucose than on ethanol and here the glucose figure is 34-fold LOWER. So the 42.7 is neither cleanly a protocol offset nor cleanly biology, and it cannot be attributed to carbon source.

the_gap_exceeds_the_whole_bruheim_datase.reading: Kozak's single ethanol number is 13-fold above the HIGHEST acetyl-CoA Kumar & Bruheim measured anywhere, across four carbon sources, batch and chemostat, and four nutrient limitations. Within the Bruheim glucose-limited series the pool moves only 9.7 to 37.1 nmol/gDW across D = 0.05 to 0.31, and the authors state there is no correlation between growth rate and pool sizes.

acetyl_coa_provenance.answer_to_the_question_asked: The two numbers do not come from different compartments, and they do not come from different units. They come from different laboratories using different quench protocols, on different carbon sources, and the cross-laboratory anchors show the discrepancy is not a uniform scale factor either. The gap is therefore unresolved as biology and resolved as provenance: it is a splice, and the repository was right to refuse to build on it.

cell_mass.verdict: PARTIALLY RESOLVED. Dry weight per cell is found, measured, in the repository's own strain, in a chemostat, with growth-rate dependence. Cytosolic volume per gram dry weight is NOT found as a measured quantity in any primary source, and remains a composition of three literature inputs from two laboratories.
cell_mass.dry_weight_per_cell: 10.6 to 17.4 pg/cell over D = 0.20 down to 0.033 h^-1, CEN.PK113-7D, galactose-limited chemostat. Sillje et al. 1999, J Bacteriol 181:396-400, PMID 9882651. See scalars[native.cell_mass.dry_weight_per_cell]. This closes the 'dry weight per cell' half of the native_data cell_mass gap, though on galactose rather than glucose limitation.
cell_mass.cytosolic_volume_per_gdw: Not measured by any source found. The repository's own description in src/ystwin/pathway/thermo_gate.py of CYTOSOLIC_VOLUMES_ML_PER_GDCW as 'A CONVENTION, not a measurement' is CORRECT and is now backed by a recorded search rather than by absence of effort. The literature-supported envelope is 0.40 to 6.6 mL/gDW; the convention (1.0, 2.0, 2.7) lies inside it.

volume_floor_is_load_bearing.claim: The repository's 1.0 mL/gDW floor is not a conservative bound. It is 1.66-fold above the point at which the thiolase refutation changes sign under the estimator the repository prefers.
volume_floor_is_load_bearing.arithmetic: eQuilibrator's threshold for r_0103 at [CoA] = 100 uM and [acetoacetyl-CoA] = 1 uM is 1414 uM. The ethanol-limited 0.85 umol/gDW reaches 1414 uM at a cytosolic volume of 0.601 mL/gDW. Below that volume the ethanol state is ABOVE threshold and the ordering the repository refuted returns.
volume_floor_is_load_bearing.under_modelseed_corrected: At the corrected ModelSEED energy the threshold is 19042 uM and the ethanol state would need a cytosolic volume of 0.045 mL/gDW to reach it, which is outside any envelope. Under that estimator the refutation is volume-independent.
volume_floor_is_load_bearing.recommendation: Record 0.601 mL/gDW as the eQuilibrator-side crossing volume rather than resting the refutation on the 1.0 floor, and let gate_across_volumes and volume_dependent_steps sweep down to at least 0.40 mL/gDW so the corner is visible rather than excluded by the range.
volume_floor_is_load_bearing.caveat: Both feeds are whole-cell pools being divided by a cytosolic volume, which overstates the cytosolic concentration. Correcting that labelling moves both states DOWN and away from the threshold, so it strengthens the refutation rather than weakening it.

unresolved.detail: No primary source was found that MEASURES cytosolic volume per gram dry weight, or intracellular water volume per gram dry weight, in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. The values in circulation are model conventions carried between modelling papers. Recorded as a searched negative, not as an absence of effort.

checked_and_rejected: Elsemman et al. 2022, Nat Commun, PMC8831649: a whole-cell model that constrains compartments by protein mass and membrane area in g protein and um^2/cell, not by mL/gDW. Carries no cytosolic volume per gram dry weight.

BioNumbers BNID 105094 'volume of cell occupied by water', 68 percent: traces to Kamihira, Taniguchi & Kobayashi 1987, a supercritical-CO2 sterilization paper on baker's yeast. A bulk water content of a commercial pressed yeast, not a growth-resolved cytosolic volume. Rejected as a source.

Boender et al. 2009, AEM 75:5607, PMID 19592533: retentostat quantitative physiology in CEN.PK113-7D. Reports biomass dry weight concentration and viability but no dry weight per cell. Rejected for this quantity.

unresolved.detail: Mitchison JM (1958), 'The growth of single cells. II. Saccharomyces cerevisiae', Exp Cell Res 15:214-221, doi 10.1016/0014-4827(58)90077-6, PMID 13574174, is the primary single-cell dry-mass source that the modern single-cell literature defers to. It is behind an Elsevier paywall with no open mirror found, so its numbers are not recorded here.
unresolved.related: Feijo Delgado F et al. 2013, PLoS One 8:e67590, PMID 23844039, measures single-cell dry mass by H2O/D2O buoyant-mass exchange and states in its own discussion that 'Budding yeast dry mass content per cell is not widely reported and growth conditions vary can vary widely', deferring to Mitchison. Its yeast dry masses appear only in Figure 3c as distributions and are not extractable as numbers from the text. Its quoted 725 fg and 179 fg medians are E. coli, not yeast; do not transcribe them as yeast values.
unresolved.impact: None on the deliverable. Sillje 1999 supplies a chemostat, growth-rate-resolved dry weight per cell in the repository's own strain, which is a better match than a batch single-cell figure would be.

unresolved.detail: Neither acetyl-CoA source is compartment-resolved, and no compartment-resolved cytosolic acetyl-CoA measurement in a CEN.PK113-7D chemostat was found. The repository therefore has no measured cytosolic acetyl-CoA at all, only two whole-cell pools. Any statement of the form 'cytosolic acetyl-CoA is X uM' in this repository is a whole-cell pool divided by an unmeasured volume.
